question: The term ‘Analysis of variance’ was introduced by:
solution:
The correct answer is** Ronald A Fisher.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ronald A Fisher:**

 
 
• Ronald A Fisher was a pioneering statistician and geneticist who introduced the term ‘Analysis of variance’ (ANOVA). ANOVA is a statistical method used to compare means of three or more samples to understand if at least one sample mean is different from the others.
 
• In a financial enterprise context, ANOVA can be used to analyze the variance in financial performance metrics across different departments, time periods, or investment portfolios.
 
• Fisher's work laid the foundation for modern statistical analysis, making it possible for financial analysts to make more informed decisions based on data.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karl Pearson:**

 
 
• Karl Pearson was a key figure in the development of statistics but is best known for Pearson's correlation coefficient, not for introducing ANOVA.
 
• His work primarily focused on correlation and regression analysis, which are also valuable tools in financial analysis but serve different purposes compared to ANOVA.
 
 
 
• **John Tukey:**
 
 
• John Tukey was a significant contributor to statistical science, known for developing the box plot and coining the term "bit" in computer science.
 
• Although his contributions are substantial, he did not introduce ANOVA.
 
 
 
• **William Sealy Gosset:**
 
 
• William Sealy Gosset, known by his pen name "Student", developed the Student's t-test, a fundamental statistical test used for small sample sizes.
 
• While his work is crucial in the realm of statistics, he did not introduce ANOVA.
